title: A nonabelian anyon violates Haag duality
abstract: We show that a superselction sector describing a single nonabelian anyon violates Haag duality, which is equivalent to the fundamental quantum-information theoretic principle of uniqueness of purifications. We provide a simple physics argument as well as a rigorous proof using sector theory, and instantiate our result concretely in Levin-Wen models. We also show that the associated ground state does not allow for quantum steering despite being a pure state. Finally, we show that this ground state violates approximate Haag duality, disproving the conjecture that all gapped ground states satisfy this condition. Our result implies that there are gapped phases of matter where Haag duality fails at every point in the phase.
summary: This theoretical paper demonstrates that the presence of nonabelian anyons in gapped quantum systems violates fundamental principles like Haag duality and the uniqueness of purifications. By analyzing the Levin-Wen model, the authors disprove the conjecture that all gapped ground states must satisfy approximate Haag duality. This suggests that topological order can host phases where fundamental locality assumptions break down.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the presence of nonabelian anyons violates fundamental principles of quantum field theory, specifically Haag duality and the uniqueness of purifications.
main_result: The authors show that a nonabelian anyon violates Haag duality and also violates approximate Haag duality, disproving a conjecture about gapped ground states.
method: The analysis uses operator algebraic techniques, constructing specific states involving nonabelian anyons and comparing their reduced density matrices across different partitions of the system.
model_or_system: The results are instantiated in the Levin-Wen models, which are built from unitary fusion categories and describe gapped topological phases of matter.
key_observables: Reduced density matrices, topological charge measurement projectors, and the failure of quantum steering.
important_parameters: The system must host nonabelian anyons and be partitioned into regions containing infinitely many degrees of freedom.
main_assumptions: The physical argument relies on the existence of a single nonabelian anyon; the rigorous proof assumes the vacuum satisfies Haag duality.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the process of constructing a state by splitting an anyon and moving a component into a separate region. Figure 2 illustrates the local splitting of an excitation in the Levin-Wen model.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first presenting a physical argument showing the violation of uniqueness of purifications, followed by a rigorous proof using sector theory, and concluding with the demonstration of approximate Haag duality failure in the Levin-Wen model.
why_interesting: This work connects abstract algebraic concepts (Haag duality) directly to the physical properties of topological phases realized in condensed matter systems, providing deep insights into the structure of ground states.
